This is an ad-hoc search requested by the user — Bartholomew Flynn is not yet in the tree. I'll search broadly first since "Bartholomew Flynn" is an uncommon name combination. Patrick is placed in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (~1845), so a sibling would likely appear nearby.

Zero results in Pennsylvania. Let me try US-wide before concluding — the surname alone anchors the query.

Zero again US-wide — unusual for an Irish name. Let me try spelling variants and a wildcard before concluding. "Bartholomew" is commonly misspelled in indexes.

Even the wildcard "Barth*" returns nothing. Let me try the Irish nickname "Batt" (common for Bartholomew in Irish records) and the surname variant "Flinn".

Still nothing. Let me check Ireland and Canada — alternate destinations for this family cohort.

Seven searches, all nil. Now I'll batch-log all of them.

Eight searches logged (log_005 – log_012), all negative. Here's what was searched and what it means:

---

## Search Results: Bartholomew Flynn

**All FamilySearch indexed searches returned zero results.** Eight variants were tried:

| log | Query | Country | Outcome |
|-----|-------|---------|---------|
| log_005 | Bartholomew Flynn | Pennsylvania | Negative |
| log_006 | Bartholomew Flynn | United States | Negative |
| log_007 | Bartolomew Flynn | United States | Negative |
| log_008 | Barth* Flynn (wildcard) | United States | Negative |
| log_009 | Batt Flynn (Irish nickname) | United States | Negative |
| log_010 | Bartholomew Flinn | United States | Negative |
| log_011 | Bartholomew Flynn | Ireland | Negative |
| log_012 | Bartholomew Flynn | Canada | Negative |

---

### What the nil means — and what it doesn't

The wildcard `Barth*` returning nothing US-wide is the most telling result: it rules out nearly every indexing variant of the given name. This is **not** evidence that Bartholomew didn't exist — it says he isn't name-indexed in FamilySearch's covered collections. Several explanations fit:

- **Died young in Ireland** before the family emigrated, leaving no indexed US record
- **Remained in Ireland** — Irish civil registration (post-1864) and church records are thinly indexed on FamilySearch
- **Appeared only in unindexed documents** — a probate will, court record, or church register that was digitized but not name-indexed; this is exactly the kind of record where Bartholomew might surface as a named sibling of Patrick
- The **hypothesis is unconfirmed** — the sibling relationship has not yet been established by a source

### Suggested next steps

1. **Full-text search** of Schuylkill County probate / estate records — if a parent's will named Bartholomew as a son or heir, it would appear in un-indexed page text rather than the name index. The active plan already includes pli_002 (probate, Schuylkill, 1860–1890), which could surface this.
2. **Ancestry** — independently indexes many of the same US census and vital collections with different transcription; a name the FamilySearch indexer mis-read would often surface there.
3. **Irish civil and church records** (post-1864 civil registration; Catholic parish registers on Registers.ie / IrishGenealogy.ie) — if Bartholomew was born in Ireland and stayed, records there are the right target.

Logging the search and updating the plan item status now.

**Collection searched:** England, Wiltshire, Church Records, 1518–1990 (FamilySearch collection 4380174)
**Query:** Job Purnell · birth 1821–1831 · Wiltshire, England · record type: birth/christening

- The record is from a primary source (parish register, not an index derivative)

**What would settle it:** The **1841 England census** would show Job living in or near Trowbridge at a stated age. If that age is consistent with an 1821 birth (i.e., age ~20), it confirms this is the same man and the 1851 census age was the inaccurate one. Only after that confirmation would extraction of this record's parentage be appropriate.

**Extraction is not offered** pending that confirmation.
